compiler_only_output.reason: include/types.h declares an empty ~Vector3(), so every automatic Vector3 in this TU odr-uses it: StatePath declares six (prev, node, diff1, diff2, scaled1, scaled2), UpdatePathModels declares node and the block-scoped diff it hands to Vec3_Sub, and RenderPathModels copies PATH_LIFT_MODEL_SCALE into the by-value local it passes to Model::Render. mwccarm therefore re-emits Vector3's vague-linkage D1 (4 bytes, bx lr, STB_LOPROC, no relocation and no caller in this object) alongside the licensed text. tools/relocs.py load_symbol_homes reports exactly one configured home for this spelling, arm9:0x020072c0 kind:function(arm,size=0x4), owned by an already-enrolled source; rombuild byte-compares this object's body against those cartridge bytes and refuses anything but byte-identical vague-linkage output before discarding the duplicate.

data_ov002_0210af2c is a 3-entry {PathLiftStateFn init, PathLiftStateFn behavior, const char *name} table, and mwccarm cannot fold its six pointer-to-member constants into .data, so it emits a file-scope static initializer plus a .ctor slot. That initializer is the cartridge's: the emitted .init section is 164 bytes and compares byte-for-byte equal to retail 0x021071f4 (__sinit_ov002_021071f4, kind:function(arm,size=0xa4)) at every one of the 164 offsets, with its seven literal-pool words carrying relocations to the same destinations the retail pool holds (0x0210aed0, 0x0210aee8, 0x0210aed8, 0x0210aef8, 0x0210aef0, 0x0210aee0 and the 0x0210af2c destination). Those cartridge bytes are already owned and reproduced by the separately enrolled shard src/__sinit_ov002_021071f4.c, which config/arm9/overlays/ov002/delinks.txt marks complete over .init 0x021071f4..0x02107298; this TU claims .text only and claims no .init or .ctor. Keeping this copy would give the module a second sinit body and a 27th .ctor slot against retail's 26, so the duplicate is discarded here while the retail function stays source-built by its own shard. The disposition is plain deadstrip rather than deadstrip-duplicate because the compiler names this symbol after the source file, and no symbols.txt row anywhere carries that spelling -- the cartridge names the same code __sinit_ov002_021071f4, so there is no configured home to compare against under the emitted name.

The four-byte .ctor slot mwccarm emits next to the file-scope static initializer above, and the only surviving reference to it. It has to go with the initializer: derive_deadstrip refuses to drop __sinit_dPathLiftActor_c.cpp while this word still points at it. Retail's counterpart is .p__sinit_ov002_021071f4 at ov002:0x0210811c, inside the .ctor run 0x021080d0..0x02108138 that config/arm9/overlays/ov002/delinks.txt declares as a module section owned by no file, so dsd supplies that word from the cartridge gap object and the retail table keeps its 26 entries. No symbols.txt row carries the file-derived spelling emitted here, so this object is homeless and takes a plain deadstrip, not deadstrip-data.

The [4b/8] licensing audit used to refuse this TU outright on two unlicensed functions with no policy; the three compiler_only_output rows above clear that stage, and tools/tubuild.py verify now reports 22/22 MATCH with 0 compiler-only policy errors (was 2) and 23 unlicensed section/symbol(s) (was 25). Home counts came from tools/relocs.py load_symbol_homes, not from grep: _ZN7Vector3D1Ev has exactly one configured home (arm9:0x020072c0), so it takes deadstrip-duplicate and rombuild byte-compares it against the cartridge; __sinit_dPathLiftActor_c.cpp and its .ctor pointer have none under the file-derived spelling the compiler assigns, so they take plain deadstrip -- the same code is the cartridge's __sinit_ov002_021071f4, already owned and reproduced by the enrolled shard src/__sinit_ov002_021071f4.c, so nothing goes unverified by dropping this TU's second copy. STILL BLOCKING PROMOTION, unchanged by this edit and deliberately not attempted here: linkcheck now stops one stage later, at the full object audit, on 23 unlicensed .data definitions (this class's own _ZTV/_ZTI/_ZTS and data_ov002_0210af2c, which the cartridge homes in ov002; the six pointer-to-member constants and three state-name strings, which no symbols.txt names; and the eight imported base-class RTTI records) plus emitted .text order -- D0 is emitted before D1 while the ROM has D1 first. Clearing those is non-text ownership work and a source-level destructor-order change, not a policy row. The recorded verification.linkcheck receipt lists every one of them.
